source_read: PMC HTML, PMC12147086 (Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2010, CD004332.pub2; 'What's new' records a correction to Analysis 1.5, diarrhoea, on 21 December 2010), read in full in my own browser tab: the first 120,000 characters with get_page_text and the remaining 118,000 with javascript_tool. Covered: abstract, plain language summary, background, methods (including the IPD methods), results (description of studies, risk of bias, effects of interventions), discussion, authors' conclusions, what's new, history, acknowledgements, appendices, the Data and analyses tables for Comparisons 1-5, characteristics of studies, differences between protocol and review, contributions, sources of support and declarations of interest. The forest-plot images were not opened; every number used here is printed in the text or the Data and analyses tables.

claims.overstatement: No overstatement of the Cochrane figures; 'is associated with' is cautious. Omissions worth adding: (1) The claim reports the industry role in the trials (17 of 24), but not that the manufacturer (Merck Serono) supplied the individual patient database and part-funded it. Nor does it mention that two authors declare honoraria from acamprosate makers or marketers: Lehert from Merck (also Lundbeck, Sanofi-Aventis); Soyka from Lipha and Forest (also Sanofi-Aventis, Essex, Eli Lilly, Prempharm, AstraZeneca). (2) 'Adults ... outpatient trials' fits all but one trial: Niederhofer 2002 treated adolescent inpatients. (3) The review's own Discussion and plain language summary say side effects did not make more people stop, but its Results and Analysis 1.15 show RR 1.35 (1.01-1.80), a significant excess. The claim correctly follows the analysis.
claims.note: Every Rösner number in the statement and magnitude matches the Data and analyses tables. Return to any drinking: RR 0.86 (0.81-0.91), 24 trials, 6172, NNTB 9.09 (6.66-14.28); the Discussion once prints 0.80-0.91 and 6.55-14.28. Cumulative abstinence duration: MD 10.94 (5.08-16.81), 19 trials, 5224, I² 94% (tau² 138.67). Recomputed: 10.94% of 30 days is about 3.3 days a month, matching the authors' 'about three additional days a month'. Return to heavy drinking: 0.99 (0.94-1.04), 6 trials, 2132, I² 0%. Post-treatment (3-12 months) return to any drinking: 0.91 (0.87-0.96), 7 trials, 1986, NNTB 12.5. Diarrhoea: RD 0.11 (0.09-0.13), 16 trials, 4486 (fixed effect; the Results text prints 0.10-0.13; this is the analysis corrected in December 2010). Drop-out because of adverse events: RR 1.35 (1.01-1.80), 19 trials, 5763. By funding (Comparison 5): fully industry-sponsored 0.88 (0.80-0.97), 11 trials, 2858; partly industry-supported 0.84 (0.78-0.89), 6 trials, 1765; non-profit 0.88 (0.81-0.96), 7 trials, 1549. The Results text misprints the non-profit value as 0.86 (0.81-0.91), the overall estimate; the claim follows the table. 11 + 6 = 17 trials run or supported by industry, matching the claim. The funding lists name Pelc 1992 in both the industry and non-profit groups, presumably one should be Pelc 1997, though the table's counts add to 24. Acamprosate vs naltrexone: return to any drinking 1.03 (0.96-1.10), 3 trials, 800; heavy drinking 1.04 (0.95-1.15). IPD sensitivity analysis: RR 0.83 (0.79-0.87). Overlap check (editors' comparison of trial names): 18 of McPheeters' 20 acamprosate any-drinking trials are among these 24; only Berger 2013 and Higuchi 2015 postdate this search. That supports 'the three reviews share most of their trials'. Participant totals differ within the review (6915 in the abstract and Discussion, 6894 in Included studies). Post-treatment trial counts are given as 7, 10 and 11 in different places.

anchors.locator: Methods > Criteria for considering studies for this review (Types of studies, participants, interventions)
anchors.extracted: Double-blind RCTs of acamprosate vs placebo or active control; alcohol dependence (DSM/ICD), with dependence over 50% of a mixed sample; treatment at least 4 weeks; any dose. Binary outcomes analysed with all randomised patients, drop-outs counted as relapsed.

anchors.locator: Data and analyses, Comparison 1 (Acamprosate versus placebo), outcomes 1-3; Results > Effects of interventions > Comparison 1, Primary and Secondary outcomes
anchors.extracted: Return to any drinking: 24 trials, 6172 participants, RR 0.86 (0.81-0.91), NNTB 9.09 (6.66-14.28). Cumulative abstinence duration: 19 trials, 5224, MD 10.94 (5.08-16.81). Return to heavy drinking: 6 trials, 2132, RR 0.99 (0.94-1.04), not significant (fixed effect 0.97, 0.92-1.03).

anchors.locator: Results > Effects of interventions > Comparison 1, Heterogeneity paragraph
anchors.extracted: Heavy drinking I² 0%; cumulative abstinence I² 94% (tau² 138.67); GGT I² 80%; return to any drinking tau² 0.01 (moderate).

anchors.locator: Data and analyses, Comparison 1, outcomes 17 and 18; Results > Effects of interventions > Comparison 1, Post-treatment outcomes
anchors.extracted: 3-12 months after treatment ended: return to any drinking RR 0.91 (0.87-0.96), 7 trials, 1986, NNTB 12.50 (9.09-25.00); continuous abstinence MD 8.92 (5.08-12.77), 9 trials, 3069.

anchors.locator: Data and analyses, Comparison 1, outcomes 5, 15, 16; Results > Effects of interventions > Comparison 1, Side effects and Drop-out paragraphs
anchors.extracted: Diarrhoea RD 0.11 (0.09-0.13), 16 trials, 4486, NNTH 9.09 (7.69-11.11), the only side effect more frequent of 38. Drop-out because of adverse events RR 1.35 (1.01-1.80), 19 trials, 5763, described in the Results as significant. Any drop-out RR 0.91 (0.83-0.99), 22 trials.

anchors.locator: Discussion > Summary of main results, 2nd paragraph; Plain language summary, 2nd paragraph
anchors.extracted: Both the Discussion and the plain language summary state that side effects did not lead to more early stopping on acamprosate, while citing or summarising RR 1.35 (1.01-1.80), an interval that excludes 1.

anchors.locator: Results > Description of studies > Included studies (Funding and design; Countries; Treatment regimen and duration); Data and analyses, Comparison 5
anchors.extracted: 11 trials sponsored, organised and run by industry for drug applications and 6 with manufacturer grants and facilities (17 of 24); 7 investigator-driven, non-profit. By funding: 0.88 (0.80-0.97), 0.84 (0.78-0.89) and 0.88 (0.81-0.96). 19 trials in Europe, 2 in the US (COMBINE, Mason 2006), 1 each in South Korea, Australia and Brazil. Patients detoxified first except in Mason 2006 (about half drinking). Outpatient except Niederhofer 2002 (adolescents, inpatient). Treatment 8 weeks to 1 year.

anchors.locator: Results > Risk of bias in included studies (Allocation; Blinding; Incomplete outcome data; Publication bias)
anchors.extracted: Sequence generation reported (adequate) in 6 of 24; adequate allocation concealment in 3 of 24 (Kiefer 2003, Mason 2006, Morley 2006); adequate blinding in 7; handling of missing binary data adequate in 19 of 24. Egger test not significant (weighted P = 0.861); slight funnel asymmetry.

anchors.locator: Data and analyses, Comparison 2 (Acamprosate versus naltrexone); Results > Effects of interventions > Comparison 2
anchors.extracted: 3 trials (COMBINE, Kiefer 2003, Morley 2006), 800: return to any drinking RR 1.03 (0.96-1.10); heavy drinking 1.04 (0.95-1.15); diarrhoea more with acamprosate (RD 0.27), nausea more with naltrexone (RD -0.08).

anchors.locator: Discussion > Agreements and disagreements with other studies or reviews, 2nd paragraph
anchors.extracted: The authors attribute their lower estimate, compared with earlier meta-analyses, to newer trials with negative results (Anton 2006, Mason 2006, Morley 2006).

anchors.locator: Methods > Data collection and analysis > Selection of studies and IPD acquisition; Sources of support; Acknowledgements; Declarations of interest
anchors.extracted: The manufacturer (Merck Serono) provided unconditioned access to an individual patient database, funded by national grants and a Merck Serono grant. Review funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF 01KG0724). Declarations: Lehert (Lundbeck, Sanofi-Aventis, Merck), Soyka (Lipha, Forest, Sanofi-Aventis and others) and Leucht (several companies) report honoraria; the other three report none.

key_findings.correction: Note checked in the study tables: Pelc 1992 is investigator-driven and non-profit; Pelc 1997 was sponsored and organised by Merck Lipha.
(8.05 + 11.35)/2 = 9.70, so the interval is not centred on the printed 9.82.
Namkoong 2003 study table: allocation concealment high risk (randomised by the principal investigator); sponsored by Whan-In Pharmaceutical.

reporting_issues.note: COMBINE study table: NIAAA funding; Lipha donated the active control substances and placebo and conducted monitoring visits. Rösner 2010a lists the same trial among industry-sponsored trials.
Data table rows 5-13 plus 14.1-14.26 give 35 rows, 34 distinct (vertigo twice).
The other-bias rows of Barrias 1997 and Besson 1998 both mention a naltrexone group in what are acamprosate-placebo trials, a copied text.

risk_of_bias.note: AMSTAR 2 low confidence: item 11 is not met, as in the companion review, and the IPD component is not reported in checkable form. The additional non-instrument flags (17 of 24 trials industry-run or supported, manufacturer-supplied outcome data, an IPD analyst with Merck honoraria) are well documented.

interpretation_gap.note: I would rate the gap substantial, not minor, on the card's own list. Both the plain language summary and the Discussion report a harm result in the opposite direction to the analysis (drop-out because of adverse events, RR 1.35, 1.01-1.80). A null primary outcome (return to heavy drinking) was demoted after data extraction and explained afterwards. 'Safe' is concluded without any serious-adverse-event outcome. And the abstract claims IPD verification that cannot be checked. A comparable direction error in the Amato 2010 abstract was rated substantial on that card; for consistency this one should be too.

missed: For claims: the Methods admit mixed samples when dependence was only the majority (over 50%), against over 90% in the companion naltrexone review. That is a small difference in population between the two Cochrane estimates the claims set side by side. The card records the 50% rule in its inclusion field, but not the contrast.

The heterogeneity paragraph implies I² above 75% for every outcome except return to heavy drinking, which would include return to any drinking, but it prints only tau² 0.01 for that outcome. The I² for the headline outcome is therefore not given numerically in the text; it is presumably in the forest-plot image, which was not read.
